questions.stem: Which amount is the same as 3 dollars and 5 cents?
questions.explanation: 5 cents is 5 hundredths of a dollar, so it goes in the second place after the point: $3.05.

distractors.C: wrote the numbers side by side

questions.stem: What is the next number in this pattern? 64, 32, 16, 8, …
questions.explanation: Each number is half of the one before. Half of 8 is 4.

questions.stem: A bottle holds 1.5 litres of water. Sam pours out 3 glasses of 250 mL each. How much water is left in the bottle?
A bakery made 156 muffins. It sold 89 in the morning and 38 in the afternoon. How many muffins were left?
questions.explanation: Sold altogether: 89 + 38 = 127. Left: 156 − 127 = 29.

distractors.A: only took away the morning sales

questions.stem: In the number 47 352, what is the value of the digit 7?
questions.explanation: The digits are 4 ten-thousands, 7 thousands, 3 hundreds, 5 tens, 2 ones. The 7 is worth 7000.

distractors.D: that is the value of a 7 in the first place

questions.stem: A bag has 9 red marbles and 1 blue marble. Lena takes one without looking. Which word best describes the chance that it is red?
questions.explanation: 9 of the 10 marbles are red, so red is very likely. It is not certain, because there is 1 blue marble.

distractors.A: there are lots of red marbles
distractors.D: that would need the same number of each

questions.stem: A square-based pyramid has how many vertices (corners)?
questions.explanation: 4 corners around the square base, plus 1 at the top: 5.

distractors.A: forgot the point at the top
distractors.C: that is the number of edges

questions.stem: Liam's birthday is on 28 March. His sister's birthday is exactly 2 weeks later. When is his sister's birthday? (March has 31 days.)
questions.explanation: 2 weeks is 14 days. From 28 March, 3 days takes you to 31 March, and 11 more days takes you to 11 April.

distractors.B: added 14 to the start of April

questions.stem: A train leaves at 15:25. What is this in am/pm time?
questions.explanation: After midday, subtract 12 from the hour: 15 − 12 = 3. So 3:25 pm.

distractors.C: it is after midday, so pm
distractors.E: 24-hour times are not written with pm

questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to 3/4?
questions.explanation: Multiply the top and bottom by 3: 3/4 = 9/12.

questions.stem: A rug is 3 m long and 2 m wide. How many square tiles, each 1 m by 1 m, would it take to cover the same area?
questions.explanation: Area = 3 × 2 = 6 square metres, so 6 tiles.

questions.stem: What number goes in the box?  □ × 8 = 100 − 36
questions.explanation: 100 − 36 = 64. Which number times 8 makes 64? 8.

questions.stem: Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: Try examples: 3 + 5 = 8, 7 + 1 = 8. Two odd numbers always add to an even number.

questions.explanation: Tallest: Mint 41 cm. Shortest: Sage 19 cm. 41 − 19 = 22 cm.

questions.stem: Mrs Lo has 75 stickers. She gives 8 stickers to each child until she can't give any more full sets of 8. How many stickers are left over?
questions.explanation: 8 × 9 = 72, so 9 children get 8 stickers. 75 − 72 = 3 left over.

distractors.A: that is the number of children

questions.stem: Ruby saves $4 every week. How many weeks will it take her to save $50?
questions.explanation: After 12 weeks she has $48, which is not enough. After 13 weeks she has $52, so she needs 13 weeks.

questions.stem: Which length is the longest?
questions.explanation: Change all to cm: 1.2 m = 120 cm, 98 cm, 115 cm, 1050 mm = 105 cm, 119 cm. The longest is 1.2 m.

distractors.C: 105 cm (a big number, but millimetres are tiny)

questions.stem: Tess has between 10 and 30 marbles. When she puts them into groups of 4, there are 3 left over. When she puts them into groups of 5, there are 2 left over. How many marbles does she have?
questions.explanation: Numbers between 10 and 30 that leave 3 when grouped in 4s: 11, 15, 19, 23, 27. Which leave 2 when grouped in 5s? Only 27 (5 × 5 + 2).
